newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Stocks to Watch Today - Oct 18.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Stocks to Watch Today - Oct 18.

text.p: Some Australian stocks to watch this morning:
* The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd A$17.27 (+0.05)

The partners in Australia's largest gas project said on Thursday they plan to spend A$6.0 billion to double production, making it Australia's largest single resources investment. Woodside said the partners in the North West Shelf gas project offshore Western Australia plan to double production capacity to 14.5 million tonnes of liquefied natural gas (LNG) a year.

MIM said on Friday that the development of the Ernest Henry copper-gold joint venture project will continue despite potential native title claims that threaten to halt the project. "Ernest Henry Mining Pty Ltd will continue to develop the mine and it will come into production later next year," MIM's public affairs manager, Collin Myers, told Reuters.

Workers at subsidiary Kennecott Corp's copper smelter in Utah went on strike on Wednesday but output was continuing, the firm's parent RTZ Corp Plc said. RTZ shares dropped 12 pence to 972-1/2 pence overnight on news that unionised workers at its ill-fated Kennecott copper smelter in Utah had gone on strike.

Australia's second largest telecommunications carrier, Optus Communications Pty Ltd, said on Thursday its shareholders were examining alternative strategies to proceed with the flotation of the company after a court decision which could potentially delay its planned float. Mayne has about 25 percent of Optus.

The Queensland government's 44 percent stake in the Bank of Queensland would not be absorbed as part of the planned merger between Metway, Suncorp Insurance and Finance, and Queensland Industry Development Corp (QIDC), a Courier-Mail newspaper report said. Bank of Queensland annual results due today.

New Zealand's Independent Newspapers Ltd said on Friday it was in negotiations to buy a "substantial shareholding" in New Zealand pay-TV operator Sky Network Television Ltd. Chairman Sir Colin Maiden made the announcement to the company's annual meeting in Wellington, where he also said trading profit was ahead of last year. INL is 49 percent owned by News Corp.

Marks & Spencer Plc said on Thursday it has targeted Australia in its development plans and would start looking for franchise partners early in 1997. "Following a lengthy feasibility study, we have decided to enter the Australian market, concentrating initially on Sydney," deputy chairman Keith Oates said in a statement.
